context:
Goal: a test-support helper (like hooks/cost_probe.py, used by 12 test files) can live in the repo without an owner act each time.
Problem (rule): the guard splits writers: builders write non-test paths, test-authors write test paths. A helper with no test cases must sit on a builder path, under a flat name `_test_<name>.py` (the repo's existing convention: lint/_test_git.py, lint/_test_temp.py; the checks match only test_, mutate_ and prove_). So helper code that tests rely on is written by a builder, not by a test-author. Only you can accept that.
Based on (read, relayed): the lane of step test-helper-has-a-home (PR #3395, draft, head 5038d21cb) read guard.py TEST_BASENAME, lint/test_windows_split.py CiCoverage and touched-tests.py, and ran the layout, landed-dirs, hook-stub, dup-names, glossary and record-slug checks on an empty probe (all pass). Via the coordinator, 04:12 CST; triage read none of it.
Departs from: main — main refuses a helper in a subfolder of a landed folder and names no way out; #3395 adds the named way out (a flat `_test_<name>.py` that a builder writes) and a record section; the lane says no check is widened.
Meanwhile: #3395 does not merge until you answer. This item does not remove the owner act for the cost helper in #3238: a role split of that one move was refused by the classifier, so item 829 (your hand move to hooks/cost_probe.py, or your typed grant of the split) still stands either way.
No option is starred: the coordinator gave no recommendation and triage has not read the diff.
Added 04:14 CST (the lane's own message, 04:13, same question; not read by triage): the lane recommends a (its words: one role creates the helper, no shared check changes). Triage does not star it: triage has not read #3395. The lane's two other options are added as c and d. Reads it cites: hooks/guard.py TEST_BASENAME is anchored ^test_, so _test_x.py is a non-test path (a builder writes it, a test-author is refused); a plain test_<name>.py helper fails lint/test_windows_split.py CiCoverage (it needs a checks.yml run step) and .github/scripts/touched-tests.py would run it as a script. The decision record builders-cannot-edit-tests would state the builder-writes-helper rule.
lastAnswer: 831: withdrawn as moot by the coordinator at 04:38 CST Nov 14, before you answered.

options.gain: Later helpers need no owner act.
options.label: Accept the flat `_test_<name>.py` name, written by a builder, as the repo's rule for a helper (PR #3395 records it)
options.lose: Helper code that tests rely on is written by a builder, not a test-author; your act on the cost helper in #3238 is still needed (item 829).

options.gain: Test-author independence stays as it is.
options.label: Keep today: every helper in a subfolder of a landed folder needs your act
options.lose: An owner act each time; #3238 stays stuck until you act on item 829; #3395 does not merge.

options.gain: The helper stays test-author code; no shared check changes.
options.label: A test-author writes the helper as test_<name>.py, with its own checks.yml run step
options.lose: Every helper needs a CI step and runs as a script, so each costs CI time (unmeasured).

options.gain: Fewer limits on where a helper may live.
options.label: Add _test_ to the skip lists of check_layout and check_hook_dup_names so a helper is exempt from those two checks (a widening of two shared checks)
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. Two shared checks widen.

short: Let a builder write test helpers at a flat _test_<name>.py name, or keep an owner act for each one?
title: May a test helper live at a flat `_test_<name>.py` name that a builder writes, as the repo's rule (a), keep an owner act per helper (b), have a test-author write it as test_<name>.py with a CI step (c), or exempt it from two shared checks (d)?
why: The guard keeps builders off test paths and test-authors off other paths, so a helper with no test cases fits neither side. Choosing a trades test-author independence for no owner act on later helpers.
